content: 1. A national education policy or strategy explicitly acknowledges Health-Promoting Schools (HPS) as a mechanism to achieve national development goals through education. It provides a structured framework for the nationwide promotion of HPS. 2. Leadership for HPS within the education sector is clearly defined and established. This leadership is supported by continuous contributions from the health sector and other relevant sectors at all levels. 3. Local governments, communities, and schools collaborate and demonstrate a formal commitment to the implementation of HPS initiatives. 4. Schools have policies or plans in place to ensure regular engagement, communication, and collaboration with stakeholders to support HPS efforts. 5. The leadership structure for HPS within schools is distributed and includes the school principal, leading teachers, administrative staff, school board members, management, school health personnel, students, parents, and caregivers. 6. HPS leaders, who are responsible for driving HPS initiatives, are provided with opportunities for in-service professional learning in leadership and HPS-related topics. 7. A system is in place to ensure regular planning, monitoring, and evaluation of the progress and performance of school governance and leadership in relation to HPS. 8. Students, parents, caregivers, legal guardians, and families are actively engaged and collaborate in all aspects of school operations related to HPS. 9. Schools establish both formal and informal partnerships with local community stakeholders, including local governments, to support HPS initiatives. 10. Members of the school leadership team work collaboratively with the school and local communities, including parents and caregivers, to plan and monitor the progress and performance of HPS partnerships. 11. The pedagogy and relationships between students and teachers, as well as among teachers themselves, within the school curriculum, promote health, positive relationships, safety, physical activity, healthy nutrition, and overall well-being. This is achieved through the development of knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behaviors within the school community. 12. School staff demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the physical, social, and psychological development of students and how these factors influence learning and behavior. 13. Training and support are provided to school staff to enhance their health literacy and to equip them with effective teaching and learning strategies that align with the HPS approach. 14. The content and delivery of the school curriculum are regularly planned, monitored for progress and performance, and revised as necessary to support health and well-being. 15. School policies ensure a safe environment for all members of the school community, aligning with national policies. This includes regular checks of equipment and resources to maintain safety in both physical and virtual environments. 16. The social-emotional environment within schools is regularly monitored, with improvements and feedback mechanisms implemented to ensure a positive atmosphere. 17. Comprehensive school health services are integrated into school policies and aligned with national regulations. These services reflect the needs and priorities of the school and local community and are adaptable to public health emergencies and emerging needs. 18. Investments are made in school infrastructure to support physical and social-emotional environments. This includes engaging local artists, parents, caregivers, and students in designing these environments. 19. Schools ensure access to teacher training and professional learning opportunities, incorporating HPS into graduate and in-service teacher standards, registration, or certification processes. 20. Formal agreements between schools (or local education departments) and health service providers ensure the delivery of comprehensive school health services. These agreements include equitable funding, resources for professional education, and coordination with primary care services. 21. Support is strengthened for the implementation of health services within schools by commissioning research, supporting school health professionals, and providing specialized training in child and adolescent health topics. 22. Schools provide support to students, parents, and caregivers to help them navigate, understand, and access school health services effectively.
